publication: New Jersey Herald News (masthead reads "New Jersey Herald News"; also self-referenced inside as "The New Jersey News")
summary: 8-page Newark weekly. Front page leads with a landlord barring Black guests, a Jim Crow theater lawsuit in Elizabeth, and Satchel Paige's baseball ban; inside pages cover Ethiopia/Haile Selassie wire news, Negro Press circulation stats, local church/club/society news, sports (Newark Eagles baseball, boxing), theatrical/nightlife ads (Kinney's Club, Dodger's Grill, Count Basie, Teddy Hill), and a Summit housing discrimination story.

incidents.what: Kenneth Worde files civil-rights suit against Skouras Liberty Theatre Corp. in Elizabeth over Jim Crow seating/admission pricing
Landlord D. A. O'Sullivan tells tenant Miss Rosen she cannot host Black friends at her Matawan apartment; City-Wide Tenants Council retains attorney to pursue legal action
Mrs. Zelly Sharp convicted of assault on relief investigator Joseph Raphael; sentencing set for May 25

Protest by Third Ward residents over dismissal of colored Douglass Park attendants results in reinstatement of Mrs. Elizabeth Mitchell after Deputy Director Ernest Masini met with Attorney Roger M. Yancey and a delegation
NAACP Montclair youth conference held at Washington Street YMCA Branch
Henry Armstrong scheduled to fight Barney Ross for welterweight title at Madison Square Garden Bowl

connections: References circulation/finance data on Black press nationally (98 newspapers, combined payroll $72,349.95) from Calvin's Digest column, citing Department of Commerce report and Charles E. Hall
Mentions Amsterdam News (Harlem) losing 'lost face' among readers per Calvin's Digest
Edward Lawson, managing editor of OPPORTUNITY (Journal of Negro Life), profiled visiting Tuskegee
References National Negro Congress and city-wide tenant organizing paralleling other NJ Black civic groups covered elsewhere in the archive
